prompt:
Create ONE polished enemy selection concept sheet for a first-person music-fantasy survival roguelite. Match the attached reference sheet's exact visual language and presentation: landscape 16:9, a clean FOUR COLUMNS by TWO ROWS grid, pale warm ivory background, thin warm gold grid dividers, eight complete full-body character concepts, generous separation, soft grounding shadows. This is a NEW roster: DO NOT copy characters or old numbers from reference. Each cell contains exactly ONE distinct character and a large dark burgundy two-digit number beneath it. No other text. Equal visual importance, no overlapping bodies, no cropped feet, props or head ornaments. Characters may be scaled within their cells for readability, not a physical scale chart.
STYLE: retro hand-painted Japanese animation translated to refined 3D cel-shaded game concept art, crisp ink contours, expressive silhouettes, decisive two/three-tone hard shadows, matte painted wood and cloth, antique brass, ivory, burgundy, midnight indigo, restrained muted teal. Charming but clearly hostile music-fantasy creatures. Not photorealistic, not chibi, not generic steampunk robots. Music theme beyond theater: enchanted acoustic instruments, rhythm beasts, resonance spirits, musical symbols. Keep anatomy buildable, detailed enough to model but not noisy. No guns, sci-fi equipment, neon equalizers, gore, stage scenery, HUD, ability labels, attacks or effects covering character anatomy. Do not give every character the same porcelain face mask; use species-specific faces and expressions.
EXACT NUMBER LAYOUT: top row 09, 10, 11, 12; bottom row 13, 14, 15, 16. Only these eight number labels.
09 GRAND-PIANO HERMIT CRAB: a squat broad hermit crab carrying a black lacquer miniature grand piano as its shell, lifted curved lid like a heavy crest, ivory keyboard across its front rim, strong wooden claws and six legs. Clearly crab anatomy, no human mask.
10 HARP STAG: elegant four-legged deer with an open golden harp arch integrated into its torso, visible taut strings between rib and back, branching ivory antlers, burgundy mane. Sweeping tall organic silhouette.
11 CYMBAL MOTH: hovering moth with two enormous thin circular antique brass cymbals as open wings, small velvet indigo segmented body, feathery antennae and tiny feet. Wing circles dominate silhouette; not a beetle.
12 OCARINA FROG: low round ceramic frog with a pale teal ocarina body, unmistakable finger holes across the back and a small mouthpiece snout, broad expressive eyes and chunky bent hind legs; glazed ceramic graphic highlights.
13 BASSOON SERPENT: long coiled woodwind serpent with mahogany bassoon segments, clearly articulated silver keys along spine and curled bocal snout, one raised flared bell hood. No legs, elegant S silhouette.
14 XYLOPHONE STEGOSAUR: friendly-menacing squat four-legged lizard with graduated marimba wooden bars across its arched back like dorsal plates, dark resonator tubes underneath, short mallet-tipped tail. Horizontal heavy animal silhouette.
15 TAMBOURINE FOX: nimble red-burgundy fox with a large open tambourine hoop forming its curled tail, paired brass jingles around the rim, ivory chest and pointed ears. Four feet, playful predatory stance; no violin or horn.
16 MUSIC-BOX BALLERINA: eerie elegant full-body porcelain clockwork dancer, delicate ivory face, burgundy pleated bell-shaped skirt opening to reveal a tiny pinned music-box cylinder at waist, small winding key behind, slender jointed legs, one raised arm. Balanced poised stance, adult proportions, no display pedestal.
Match reference palette and rendering closely, while all eight silhouettes must be distinct and new.
